solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Confuse dance partner, incorporating curtsy (extremely unusual)

parts.note: a disco is a dance or dance party

indicators.note: incorporating means the partner word takes the following letters into its body

parts.note: a mate is a partner
a bob is a quick curtsy or bow

indicators.note: extremely asks for only the outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A dancer is thrown off when their partner suddenly drops into a curtsy, which is most unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(extremely unusual)' reads as an aside on the curtsy but supplies the two end letters of 'unusual'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to bewilder or throw someone into a state of muddle; the answer is a jocular synonym.

clue.text: Way to get fresh water — an initial dose's spoiled

indicators.note: spoiled suggests the letters of the phrase are ruined and so reworked

explanation.surface: A water-treatment process goes wrong because the first dose of chemicals was bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' shuffles the letters of AN INITIAL DOSE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing the salt from seawater is a process for producing drinkable fresh water.

clue.text: Taser possibly wounded one in the provinces

parts.note: stung means hurt or wounded
'un is a dialect form of one, as spoken in rural regions

explanation.surface: A Taser may have injured someone out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks Taser as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a brand of electroshock weapon that immobilises its target.

clue.text: Presumably, only upright text stradding line, nothing inverted or swinging

indicators.note: inverted means the whole assembled string is turned back to front
stradding (straddling) means the text phrase sits on either side of the next letter

parts.note: text printed only upright would presumably have no italics, giving NO ITALICS
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A typographic musing: upright text over a line, with nothing upside down or tilted.
explanation.walkthrough: NOITALICS goes round L, O is added, and 'inverted' reverses the lot: ONOITALLICS becomes the answer. The clue prints 'stradding' for straddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging back and forth is a regular to-and-fro movement, the noun naming such motion.

clue.text: Forbid Scotch bonnet for poultry

definitions.note: the definition is a collective noun; the answer is one kind of fowl

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
a tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish woollen bonnet

explanation.surface: A cook is banned from using Scotch bonnet chillies on the chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch bonnet' looks like the chilli pepper but is the Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breed of domestic chicken, so a kind of farmyard fowl.

clue.text: Some self-controlled robbers turning over disorderly house

indicators.note: turning over means the picked letters are read backwards
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Some disciplined thieves change their ways at a rowdy establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: OLLEDROB runs through 'controlled robbers' and is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly house is the legal term for a brothel, which this Italian word names.

clue.text: Brief feeble strike

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble one

explanation.surface: A short, weak industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' trims LAME to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam is an informal verb for hitting or thrashing someone.

clue.text: European capital's unbelievable hotel

parts.note: a tall story is an unbelievable one
an inn is a hotel or hostelry

explanation.surface: A tourist raves about an incredible hotel in a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbelievable' is TALL as in a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Estonia, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Book genuine article at great cost, in good time

parts.note: right as in the right stuff, the genuine article
an is the indefinite article
dearly means at a high price

explanation.surface: Reserve the real thing even if it costs a lot, but do it early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'genuine article' reads as one phrase, the real thing, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means very early in the morning, so promptly and with time to spare.

clue.text: Dash this way to increase cheating

parts.note: so means in this way
to up is to increase
a con is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A sprinter is urged to step up the cheating this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb but is a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash in cookery is a tiny quantity, a trace or slight touch.

clue.text: Memory, sadder, leaving university — but I digress

definitions.note: the phrase is what one who wanders off topic says, standing for such a person

parts.note: RAM is computer memory

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the word

parts.note: bluer means more melancholy

explanation.surface: A sad recollection of leaving college, before the speaker wanders off topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes U out of BLUER. The definition is something said by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks discursively and wanders off topic would say these words.

clue.text: Stage prop

definitions.meaning: a stage of a journey or race is a section of it
a support, as a table stands on one

explanation.surface: A piece of theatre furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a relay is one sense; a supporting limb of furniture is the other.

clue.text: A card after open country doctor's farewell

indicators.note: after places the card part behind the country and doctor pieces

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or open grassland
a vet is an animal doctor
a king is a court card

explanation.surface: A rural doctor deals a card as a way of saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' moves 'A card' behind the country and doctor pieces, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying goodbye before departure is a formal synonym for a farewell.

clue.text: Sort that's content in mountain blunder

indicators.note: in means the inner letters go inside the mountain and blunder pieces

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
betise is a foolish blunder or stupid remark, from French

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inner letters, without the outside ones

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out what is contained in a mountaineering mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The blunder is the French loanword bêtise, a piece of foolishness, found in English dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort into order by letter, as in a dictionary or index.

clue.text: Fondant with centre removed could be good for dieter?

indicators.note: could be signals that the remaining letters may be arranged into something else
the middle letter of the seven-letter word is taken away

explanation.surface: Fondant without its heart might make a sweet suitable for slimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with centre removed' takes D out, leaving FONANT, and 'could be' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Food free of fat is suited to someone trying to lose weight.

clue.text: Park not at all limited by narrow opening: it's easily undone

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in on either side by the next piece

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening
PK is the abbreviation for park
no means not at all

explanation.surface: A park sits squeezed into a narrow gap, and the arrangement does not hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park not' looks like part of a phrase but splits into an abbreviation and a negation.
explanation.definitionFit: A running knot that slips and can be untied with a single pull.

clue.text: Quickly deal with water source in watercourse

indicators.note: in means the spring goes inside the channel

parts.note: a ditch is a channel for water
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A farmer quickly sorts out a spring rising in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: A spa is a spring of mineral water, the source a resort is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle or finish off a task promptly; also to kill swiftly.

clue.text: Island lair overlooking more than one lake disturbed Corsican neighbour

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out the lakes from the pool of letters
disturbed means the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is lake, so two of them are LL

explanation.surface: An island den above several lakes is upset, near Corsica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' removes LL from ISLANDLAIR and 'disturbed' rearranges ISANDAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian island lies just south of Corsica across the Strait of Bonifacio.

clue.text: Misreading of Riot Act that may come from Italian press?

definitions.text: that may come from Italian press

indicators.note: a misreading jumbles the letters of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A garbled Riot Act appears in the Italian newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian press' looks like the newspapers but is a cheese press.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft Italian whey cheese, the kind of product that comes out of a cheese press.

clue.text: Dissolute person is to continue in poverty?

parts.note: want is poverty or need
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A question of whether a debauchee must keep living in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: To go on in want would be to want on, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A promiscuous or immoral person, the adjective used as a noun.

clue.text: One must yield to Madame in drag bar

indicators.note: yielding means giving up its place to the other piece

parts.note: to trail is to drag along
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drag queen gives way to a Madame in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must yield to' swaps I in TRAIL for MME.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to hamper or restrict, just as a barrier impedes.

clue.text: Most of innermost group stays

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the core is the innermost part
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Most of the inner circle remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' looks like a verb but is the bones of a corset.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays was the old name for a stiffened bodice, the boned undergarment.

clue.text: Luddite's letter about central heating and new work surface for cooking

indicators.note: about means the letter's name goes around the following pieces

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T
op is short for opus, a work
a hob is a cooktop

explanation.surface: A Luddite writes a letter complaining about central heating and a new cooker top.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is spelt out as its name, and 'work' is the musical opus.
explanation.definitionFit: The original Luddites smashed machinery; the term now means someone who fears or resists new technology.

clue.text: Wonder initially at writer's empathy

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Amazement at the way an author can feel for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling of reverent wonder and amazement is a direct synonym.

clue.text: One rejected players unsuitable for closet drama?

parts.note: actors who are openly out of the closet would not suit a closet drama, so they are out
the cast is the set of players in a show

explanation.surface: A rejected actor is one of a company unfit for a play meant to be read rather than staged.
explanation.walkthrough: A closet drama is a play meant for reading, not performance; 'out' puns on coming out of the closet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah, someone cast out or shunned by society.

clue.text: No matter which area, state half of its capital

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: Pick any region; the state's capital is split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of its capital' is a confirming extra: the answer is also the second half of Albany, capital of New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a determiner meaning whichever one, without restriction.

clue.text: Gentle heating retains hot glow

indicators.note: retains means the cooking word holds the letter inside

parts.note: simmering is cooking over a low heat

explanation.surface: A pan on a low flame keeps its heat and gives off a glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts H inside SIMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft wavering light or gleam, a gentle glow.

clue.text: Boy repeating year keeps talking like vacant woman with inferior lover

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: keeps means the pair holds the following letters between them
repeating means the year letter appears twice

parts.note: chatter is idle talking

indicators.note: vacant means the word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A boy kept back a year chats on like an airhead about a woman and her lowly lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy repeating year' suggests a pupil kept down at school, but 'repeating' doubles the year letter. Lawrence's heroine takes the gamekeeper Mellors, her social inferior, as lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of D H Lawrence's novel has an affair with her husband's gamekeeper.
